chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it upon the Imam that he should make those behind him hear, even if they are numerous?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him recite a moderate recitation.'
And do not raise your voice in your prayer, nor conceal it, but seek a way between that.

key_terms.وَلَا تَجْهَرْ بِصَلَاتِكَ: And do not raise your voice in your prayer
key_terms.وَلَا تُخَافِتْ بِهَا: Nor conceal it (be silent with it)

ai.seo_question: What is the appropriate volume for an Imam's recitation during congregational prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential standard for congregational recitation, defining 'moderate' (wasatan) as audibility for those directly behind the Imam rather than a fixed decibel level. It explicitly links this practical ruling to the Quranic principle of avoiding both excessive loudness and complete silence, ensuring the recitation serves its communal function without distraction. This interpretation reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam's role in facilitating collective worship through balanced vocal projection.
